messages:
alejandra: Heads-up — v7 canary on slice `enterprise-long` is showing signal divergence vs v6. Not massive but consistent across a few metrics. See quick numbers below, linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood/exp/175001

mike: Numbers? short summary please

alejandra: OK — summary from the last 30m (15% traffic): semantic-f1 delta = -2.8% (v7 vs v6), hallucination rate up from 0.4% -> 1.3%, p99 latency +65ms, kv-cache miss % jumped 5% -> 12%. Long-doc queries (token_count > 1024) account for 72% of errors.

jamal: Sounds like a length-conditioned regression, probably a decoding/kv interaction. Is this uniform across prompts or specific templates?

alejandra: Mostly on summarization and long-QA templates. Short chat and embeddings slices look fine.

sarah: If hallucination is at 1.3% that's above our usual tolerance for enterprise docs. I propose we enable an autofallback gate with conservative thresholds: either semantic-f1 drop >= 3% OR hallucination >= 1% OR p99_latency >= 60ms, trigger immediate rollback of canary to previous variant for that slice.

tanya: Do we want OR vs AND? OR is aggressive but safer. Also we should guard against noisy spikes causing flapping.

mike: I vote OR but require sustained signal: 3 consecutive 15m windows for the semantic-f1 / latency conditions, but hallucination single-window can be immediate (it's a higher-severity signal). Also only if canary traffic >= 5% for that slice.

jamal: Add exponential backoff for re-promote attempts to avoid oscillation. Suggest smoothing via moving median over the 3 windows rather than raw instantaneous values.

sarah: Agreed. Draft gate config (we can iterate):

```yaml
canary_gate:
  slice: enterprise-long
  min_traffic_pct: 5
  windows: 15m
  sustained_windows: 3
  metrics:
    - name: semantic-f1
      comparator: delta_le
      threshold: -3%
      sustain: true
    - name: p99_latency_ms
      comparator: ge
      threshold: 60
      sustain: true
    - name: hallucination_rate_pct
      comparator: ge
      threshold: 1.0
      sustain: false
  action: immediate-fallback
  backoff_on_repromote_minutes: 30
```

alejandra: Nice. Also add an allowlist for legacy customers (we have 3 tenants pinned to v6 for regulatory reasons) so they don't get auto-switched.

tanya: Good call. Also add a small safety to avoid triggering on tiny absolute sample counts: require > 200 queries in the window to evaluate hallucination signal.

mike: Summing up: OR semantics with sustain for f1/latency (3x15m median), hallucination single-window but sample size >200, min traffic 5%, backoff 30m. Who's owning the rollout update?

alejandra: I'll push the gate change and bootstrap a 1h shadow run with 10% traffic to confirm. If the gate fires we'll immediate rollback and alert SRE + product.

deploy-bot: canary_gate/config updated at commit abc1234 by alejandra.

jamal: I'll dig into kv-cache miss patterns and tokenization edgecases in the next 2hrs, will post quick findings.

sarah: I'll add a small eval harness for long-doc deterministic prompts to surface more systematic delta and attach to the canary dashboard.

tanya: OK, implement and observe. If anything crosses the hallucination line we abort and open an incident. :exclamation:

alejandra: Thanks — updating rollout now and will ping once shadow is complete.

deploy-bot: gate deployed to canary controller (sha: abc1234) at 1750012378. Monitoring enabled: enterprise-long slice.

jamal: Noted, starting tracing on kv-paths now.

alejandra: Closing loop — will post results in #eng-ml once we have 30/60/120m snapshots. Thanks all.
